transcript.text: I can certainly help with that. 'Not working properly' covers quite a few possibilities, but the most common and easiest to fix are usually settings-related. Firstly, many modern hobs have a child lock (often indicated by a key or padlock symbol on the display) which disables the controls. If this is active, the hob will not respond to your inputs. Secondly, if you have an induction hob, it only works with specific magnetic cookware; using the wrong pan can make it seem like the zone isn't working. Could you tell me two things? First, is there a key or padlock symbol on the control panel that might be lit up (indicating a child lock is on)? Second, do you know if your hob is ceramic/induction (flat glass top) or gas/electric coil?
No padlock or key showing that I can see. It's a ceramic hob, flat glass top with touch controls, Zanussi. Only one of the rings isn't working, the rear right one.

Thanks. Since it's a Zanussi ceramic hob and only one zone (rear right) is dead, we can narrow this down. 1. 2. 3. The power module controlling that specific zone has failed (less common, but possible). 1. Wipe the entire hob surface, especially around the rear right controls and the glass area, with a dry cloth to ensure no moisture is interfering with the touch sensors.
2. Try turning on just the rear right zone again. Does it show an error code (like E05 or similar) on the display? If not, leave it on for 30 seconds and carefully place your hand near the glass where the ring should be—is there any warmth at all? Let me know what happens.
Wiped it down and tried again. No error code, the number shows fine on that zone. Left it 30 seconds and no warmth I could feel, and it doesn't glow red at all.

On a ceramic hob like yours, the most likely cause is that the radiant heating element under the glass for the rear right zone has failed (burnt out). A less common possibility is the energy regulator (the component that controls power to that ring) has failed. Unfortunately, fixing this requires removing the glass top to access and test or check the element. This involves disconnecting the mains supply and carefully lifting the heavy glass surface, which carries a risk of breaking it if not done correctly. Because this is an internal repair involving live electrical components under a fragile surface, I recommend calling in a qualified appliance engineer to check the element for you.
